title: Notre histoire (FFF institutional history, including INF/Centre National du Football Clairefontaine)
notes: Located via WebSearch as the FFF's own institutional-history page, which should cover the Centre National du Football / INF Clairefontaine. WebSearch summaries from other sources (French and English Wikipedia articles on INF Clairefontaine / Centre technique national Fernand-Sastre, not this FFF page) independently corroborate the 1988 founding: the Centre National du Football (INF Clairefontaine) was inaugurated 11 June 1988 by President Mitterrand, with FIFA president João Havelange present, after the INF Vichy cohort relocated there in January 1988; it was restructured into a 13-16 pre-training centre in 1990 under DTN Gérard Houllier. title: Inverting the Pyramid: The History of Football Tactics
author: Jonathan Wilson
notes: Jonathan Wilson's 'Inverting the Pyramid' (Orion, UK, first published 2009; also published by Nation Books in the US, and a fully revised 15th-anniversary edition exists) is a genuine, widely-cited book covering the history of football tactics, including a chapter-level treatment of Italian catenaccio and Arrigo Sacchi's shift to zonal-marking, high-pressing football at Milan in the late 1980s — this matches the entry's brief well on search-snippet evidence. I could not confirm exact page-level claims, nor find/confirm a URL for a specific standalone Jonathan Wilson article (e.g. in The Guardian's 'The Question' column) about catenaccio specifically; two dated Wilson Guardian 'Question' columns turned up in search (22 Sept 2009 on the sweeper's possible return; 23 Dec 2009 on the next decade of tactics) but neither is confirmed to be centrally about catenaccio/Sacchi, and I did not fabricate a more specific-sounding URL. WebFetch on the Orion Books publisher page returned HTTP 403 in this environment (same session-wide WebFetch outage), so even the publisher's own description of the book's contents was not read by me.
comment: Book's existence, author, publisher and general subject matter (football tactics history including catenaccio/Sacchi) are corroborated by multiple independent search results, but I have not read any primary text confirming the entry's specific supports claims (1982/2006 World Cup wins, Euro 2020, the late-1980s zonal-marking reform) are addressed in this book with correct dates. Also unaddressed: the entry note's caution against reducing 'Italian football' to a single stereotype — not confirmed one way or the other. Keep as placeholder; a follow-up session should fetch the publisher page or a detailed table-of-contents/review to confirm scope, and separately verify the tournament-win dates (1982, 2006, Euro 2020) against a results source.
